tasks.title: Add createPartnerMentionBatchSchema with the per-channel URL rule
tasks.description: The batch body schema (spec §7): { mentionedAt, internalNote?, entries: [{ channel, url? }] } with entries min length 1. A refinement on EACH entry requires url for INSTAGRAM/FACEBOOK/TWITTER/YOUTUBE/TIKTOK/NEWSLETTER and allows it absent for WHATSAPP/OTHER (AC-8, closes OQ-3). Note: batchId is NOT part of the body — it is server-generated (R-5). Tests: one case per branch of the rule (8 channels, required-vs-optional), a multi-entry happy path, and an explicit assertion that a client-supplied batchId is stripped/rejected. DONE: partnerMentionEntrySchema is .pick({channel,url}) off the entity + a superRefine that attaches the error to the ['url'] path (so the admin form with N url inputs can show it on the right one). Body = {mentionedAt, internalNote?, entries[min 1]}; partnerId comes from the URL path, batchId is server-generated — both absent from the shape and stripped by Zod. 36 tests. IMPORTANT for T-009: the R-5 guarantee holds only if the service inserts from the PARSED output; building an insert from the raw body bypasses the stripping entirely.

subtasks.title: Batch body schema with entries array
Test client batchId is not accepted

tasks.title: Add update and search schemas for partner mentions
tasks.description: updatePartnerMentionSchema (single-row correction: channel/mentionedAt/url/internalNote, all optional) and searchPartnerMentionSchema (partnerId, channel filter, date range, pagination). Admin list uses page+pageSize, never limit. Tests: partial update parses; search rejects unknown params. DONE: two files following the entity convention — partner-mention.update.schema.ts and partner-mention.admin-search.schema.ts. 24 tests. The update schema carries a superRefine: a patch switching channel to a permalink channel MUST carry the url in the same request, because the schema never sees the stored row and a bare switch would turn a urlless WHATSAPP row into a urlless INSTAGRAM one. partnerId and batchId are NOT patchable (moving/regrouping is not a correction). Search extends AdminSearchBaseSchema (page+pageSize, never limit) and declares channel, batchId, mentionedAfter/mentionedBefore — the last two range over mentioned_at, distinct from the inherited createdAfter/createdBefore over created_at.

tasks.title: Create PartnerMentionModel extending BaseModel
tasks.description: packages/db/src/models/partner/partner-mention.model.ts extending BaseModel, with findByPartner (newest-first) and findByBatch. Soft-delete by default. Tests: packages/db/test/integration/partner-mention.model.integration.test.ts — insert, cascade delete when the parent partner is hard-deleted, newest-first ordering, soft-deleted rows excluded. DONE: createMany (takes the caller's tx — batch is all-or-nothing and the notification must fire post-commit), findByPartner (filters + pagination), findByBatch. 19 integration tests, all green against real Postgres. ORDERING DEFECT FOUND BY MUTATION: Postgres now() is TRANSACTION-scoped, so every row of one batch shares created_at to the microsecond. The original tie-break (mentionedAt, createdAt) was therefore NOT total and pagination could repeat a row; fixed by appending id. findByBatch's original asc(createdAt) could not express insertion order at all — replaced by asc(channel), which uses the pg enum DECLARATION order and reads the same in every batch. Two tests passed by luck before this was found; they now set createdAt explicitly / insert out of enum order.

subtasks.title: Total ordering (id tie-break) for stable pagination

tasks.title: PartnerMentionService.createBatch — N rows, one transaction, server-side batchId
tasks.description: packages/service-core/src/services/partner/partner-mention.service.ts, kept SEPARATE from PartnerService (mirrors partner_subscriptions getting its own schema). createBatch writes one row per entry inside a single transaction, generating one shared batchId when entries.length > 1 and leaving it null for a single entry. The batchId is generated INSIDE the service — never read from input (R-5). Returns the created rows. Permission check via PermissionEnum.PARTNER_MANAGE, Result<T> return. DONE: extends BaseCrudService (repo convention) with PARTNER_MANAGE on every hook. batchId minted inside the method, null for a single entry. Notification is a PartnerMentionNotifyPort (mirrors PartnerRevokeNotifyPort) fired once per batch, after the write, with every failure swallowed. TWO INHERITED PATHS SEALED: create() throws (a generic single-row create yields no batchId and no notification — an orphan the partner is never told about) and _executeSearch/_executeCount throw (the search schema declares no partnerId, so a generic search spans every partner's log). 13 tests; mutation-verified (per-row notification + null batchId turns 4 red).

tasks.title: PartnerMentionService — list, update, soft-delete
tasks.description: Add listForPartner (paginated, newest-first), update (single row correction), and softDelete to PartnerMentionService (closes OQ-6: mentions are editable, unlike social_publish_logs). Plus listForOwner for the partner-facing read path, resolving the partner from partners.ownerUserId and returning rows grouped by batchId with internalNote omitted. MUST re-validate the MERGED row on update: updatePartnerMentionSchema can only see the patch, so `{url: null}` with no channel field is legal to it while being illegal for a stored INSTAGRAM row. That gap is the service's to close (HOS-377 T-007 note). DONE: listForPartner (admin, takes the partner explicitly so an unscoped query is unreachable), listForOwner (ownership fails closed; strips admin fields via a DELETE derived from PARTNER_MENTION_ADMIN_ONLY_MASK, NOT a schema parse — hardening a read contract 500s the whole log on one legacy row), correct (re-validates the MERGED row, closing the T-007 gap) and remove (soft only). 21 tests.
